cia.body_append:
## 'The Church Committee reforms are undone' (September 2022)

On the 20 September 2022 [Roundtable](/wiki/john-kiriakou) — the 75th anniversary of the [CIA](/wiki/cia)'s creation — [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said the reforms the [Church Committee](/wiki/church-committee) had imposed on the agency in the mid-1970s had *"just Fallen by the wayside"* twenty-one years after 9/11. The CIA, he said, now runs *"an active assassination programme,"* refuses even to acknowledge the existence of the drone programme, ran *"a secret prison system around the world,"* and carries out international kidnappings *"they euphemistically call renditions."* Kiriakou called for the creation of *"a new Church Committee"* — a demand he attributes to *"some important people"* — as the only remaining institutional check on the agency.<Cite t="02:47" /><Cite t="03:18" /><Cite t="03:49" /><Cite t="04:19" />

## 'Butts in seats' — the contractor economy

Kiriakou characterises modern CIA staffing as heavily dependent on *"butts in the seats"* — his shorthand for CIA-inside contractors from [Booz Allen Hamilton](/wiki/mass-surveillance) and SAIC who *"don't really work for the CIA"* but *"punch information into a computer"* or run clandestine programmes on the agency's behalf. The agency, he said, *"doesn't have to pay for their health insurance or their pension contribution and everybody's happy,"* while *"there's no accountability, there's nobody that has to answer to anyone."* Kiriakou tied the arrangement to the observation that Washington, DC now has *"more millionaires per capita"* than *"anywhere else in America, including Silicon Valley"* — *"and it's not an accident."*<Cite t="04:51" /><Cite t="05:23" /><Cite t="05:55" />

barack-obama.body_append:
## The 'nixonian' obsession with leaks

On the [Roundtable](/wiki/john-kiriakou) in September 2022, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) said friends who worked inside the [Obama](/wiki/barack-obama) White House had described the president's obsession with prosecuting national-security leaks in terms he called *"nixonian."* Kiriakou tied the fixation to the failed initial attempt to install [John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan) as [CIA](/wiki/cia) director in 2009: progressives *"just threw a fit,"* Brennan was withdrawn, and — on the account Kiriakou heard — Obama began compensating by taking the aggressive line on leaks Brennan and Brennan's allies wanted.<Cite t="19:06" /><Cite t="19:38" />

john-brennan.body_append:
## 'A shyster, drug dealer almost' (September 2022)

On [Gonzalo Lira's Roundtable](/wiki/john-kiriakou) in September 2022, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) offered one of his sharpest personal descriptions of [John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan). Prefacing it with a self-description — *"I'm politically conservative and very conservative"* — Kiriakou said Brennan *"looks like a shyster, drug dealer almost — I would trust him as far as I could throw him, to tell you the truth."* He restated the [origin story](/wiki/john-brennan) that runs through the corpus: Brennan's rescue from Martha Kessler's dismissal by the [George Tenet](/wiki/george-tenet) *"rabbi"* relationship, and Brennan's subsequent settling of scores by having Kessler fired in turn.<Cite t="20:08" /><Cite t="20:39" /><Cite t="23:12" />

julian-assange.body_append:
## Kiriakou on why the CIA pursues him (2022)

On Gonzalo Lira's [Roundtable](/wiki/john-kiriakou) in September 2022, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) explained the [CIA](/wiki/cia)'s pursuit of [Julian Assange](/wiki/julian-assange) as *"twofold."* First, he said, Assange was *"doing it with impunity"* — actively soliciting leaks, offering protection, and *"taking people's personal security very seriously"* by redacting to protect the identities of individuals named in the underlying documents, a level of tradecraft that *"just enraged"* the agency. Second, Kiriakou said, the 2017 [Vault 7](/wiki/vault-7) release was the moment that *"pushed the agency over the edge"*: those documents were *"the most sensitive, most important crown jewels perhaps ever in the history of the CIA — that was just too much for them, bridge too far."*<Cite t="34:37" /><Cite t="35:08" />

john-kiriakou.body_append:
## Self-description: 'politically conservative and very conservative'

On Gonzalo Lira's [Roundtable](/wiki/john-kiriakou) in September 2022, in the middle of a running exchange with [Ray McGovern](/wiki/ray-mcgovern) and the New Zealand activist Suzie Dawson, [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) volunteered an on-the-record self-description that has since become useful shorthand across the corpus: *"I'm politically conservative and very conservative — and I think that [John Brennan](/wiki/john-brennan) is just, you know, he looks like a shyster, drug dealer almost. I would trust him as far as I could throw him."*<Cite t="20:08" /> Earlier in the same conversation he offered a corresponding religious self-description: *"I'm a lapsed Catholic; I have found it's easier to ask for forgiveness than permission."*<Cite t="28:23" />
